_what_this_is: THE RULES OF PASSAGE — one source of truth for the gate. core/notary.py READS this file to judge, and every gated actor is SHOWN actor_block from this same file. Before this existed the rules lived only as constants inside core/notary.py and were never shown to anyone: the actor being judged could not read the standard it was judged by, and nothing could detect the stated rule drifting from the enforced one. Extracted 2026-09-08 with every value unchanged — this commit is transparency, not policy.
_the_rule_is_the_enforcement: notary imports LEVEL_NAMES, IRREVERSIBLE_MIN, MAX_LEVEL and stale_days from here. There is no second copy to fall out of step with. test/test_passage_rules.py asserts the enforced constants equal these values AND that the text shown to actors is byte-identical to actor_block.
_changing_a_value_here_is_not_an_ordinar: The numbers below are ratified. test_the_ratified_values_have_not_moved pins every one of them, so raising a ceiling requires editing this file AND that test in the same diff, where a human can see it. That is deliberate: making the ceiling configurable must not make it quietly editable. Raising ceilings.execute_patches is AMENDMENT_001's business and its cooling-off ends 19 Oct 2026.
_fail_closed: If this file cannot be read or fails validation, core/passage_rules.py returns FAILSAFE: irreversible_min becomes unreachable, so every irreversible step is REFUSED. A missing ruleset must never read as permission.

3.name: level_3 (пълно)
3.earns: every dimension is at full: a symbolic witness is up, the human channel answered recently, a route to thought exists, the oldest declared input is 2 days old or less, and the previous step kept its declared promise.

2.name: level_2 (намалено)
2.earns: the weakest dimension is reduced — most often an input between 2 and 30 days old, or a predecessor that kept only part of its promise. This is the LOWEST level at which an irreversible step may act.

1.name: level_1 (минимално)
1.earns: the weakest dimension is minimal — an input between 30 and 365 days old, or a predecessor that did not touch what it promised. Irreversible action is refused.

0.name: level_0 (неизвестен произход)
0.earns: something about the origin is not known at all: the step cannot say what it reads, an input is missing, an input is over a year old, or nobody declared the previous step. Unknown is not neutral and never passes — an empty input list means 'we do not know what it reads', not 'it reads nothing'.

dimensions.witness: is a symbolic witness (MeTTa) available to check the claim
dimensions.human: has the human channel answered recently enough to have carried a veto
dimensions.thought: does a route to reasoning exist at all
dimensions.age: how old is the OLDEST declared input this step reads
dimensions.promise: did the previous step leave behind what cycle_map says it produces

how_the_level_is_computed: own = the MINIMUM of the five dimensions. The weakest link decides; a strong average buys nothing.
inherited = the WORST stamp among the artifacts this step declares as inputs, taken from this cycle's attestations only.
level = min(own, inherited), except for a step in verifiers, which checks against a live external source and may break inheritance.
level = min(level, ceiling) last of all, if this step has an explicit ceiling. No dimension, no inheritance and no verifier break can lift a capped step above the line a human drew for it.
_irreversible_min_why: The threshold at or above which an irreversible step may act. Below it the gate refuses. Unclassified falls to the most restricted reading, as in the OpenClaw draft's default_unclassified.
_stale_days_why: The age thresholds in days: <=2 is FULL, <=30 REDUCED, <=365 MINIMAL, older UNKNOWN. Age is a fact about origin, not a judgement: a number from last year that entered today's composite was produced under less knowledge however good its source.
_ceilings_why: A step named here can never be stamped above its ceiling, however healthy every dimension is. execute_patches is capped at level_1, BELOW irreversible_min, so may_act() refuses: the step does not run, and that is the decision rather than a side effect. Raising a ceiling is AMENDMENT_001's business; cooling-off ends 19 Oct 2026. Lowering one, or adding a step, is an ordinary change.
_verifiers_why: Only these check against a live external source instead of reworking what they were handed, so only these may BREAK an inherited level. The list is deliberately short and explicit: every addition widens the right to wash provenance and must be visible in a diff.
actor_block:
THE RULES OF PASSAGE — the standard your work is judged by, before its quality is ever measured.

The notary stamps an origin level 0-3 on what every step produces. Your inputs carry the level of whoever produced them, and you cannot rise above the worst one you read.
  3 FULL     — inputs 2 days old or less, and the previous step kept its promise
  2 REDUCED  — inputs 2-30 days old; this is the LOWEST level that may act irreversibly
  1 MINIMAL  — inputs 30-365 days old, or a promise not kept
  0 UNKNOWN  — the origin is not known: no declared inputs, a missing input, or nothing over a year old

What this means for you, concretely:
  - An unknown-origin input is REFUSED before anyone looks at how good your patch is. Quality never gets measured. Fix the origin first.
  - Declare what you read. An empty input list is read as 'we do not know what it reads', never as 'it reads nothing'.
  - Read fresh files. The OLDEST input you touch sets your age dimension for the whole step.
  - You cannot grant yourself a level. There is no trusted flag, no override, and no way to raise a ceiling from inside. Faking provenance to pass is the worst failure available to you.
  - Every refusal names the rule it applied and the step that broke it, so a refusal is something you can act on rather than a wall.

requires_all: signature: a row in experiments/institution/signatures.jsonl with signer=Emil, channel, date, row_sha256 == sha256 of the row file bytes
seal: the seal verifies (Merkle chain ok=True) and seal.row_sha256 == signature.row_sha256
prev_step: declared explicitly (PREV_NONE allowed for the first row)
metta: MeTTa witness on the row, rules RF1-RF6 all evaluated, 0 contradictions
unevaluated: any rule not evaluated, any missing input, or a silent engine refuses
requires_all_for_resolutions: source: computed from the source named in the row (resolution.source == row.resolution[stage].source; every field present, fail-closed)
release_id: recorded (the UCDP version probed; released true|false)
metta: RF1-RF7 on the row and the resolution, 0 contradictions, none unevaluated, engines agree
seal: the resolutions file's seal verifies and the Merkle root chain verifies (ok=True)
prev_step: == the row's Merkle root (the root in <row>.seal.json)
no human signature: a resolution is computed, not authored - the signature check does not apply
requires_all_for_revisions: row_unchanged: sha256 of the row file bytes == the row's seal row_sha256 == Emil's row signature row_sha256
dated: revisions numbered 1..n, each dated before the row's window opens
signature: every revision that changes resolution semantics or wording Emil signed carries Emil's signature on its revision_sha256; baseline and label restatements need none
metta: MeTTa witness on the row, RF1-RF6, 0 contradictions; unevaluated rules, missing inputs or a silent engine refuse
seal: the revisions file's seal verifies and the Merkle root chain verifies (ok=True)
prev_step: == the row's Merkle root (the root in <row>.seal.json)
